selection_bias_summary: Rebuilt 2026-08-18 against PINNED OpenAlex source ids, each verified by exact display_name before any work was pulled. The 2026-06 build resolved journals by name against a resolver that took the first fuzzy hit, which returned International Review of Economics & Finance for 'Review of Finance'; that resolver is fixed and this build does not resolve by name at all. In-field (finance) counts: 55 top3_finance, 31 strong_field, 20 stalled. CLASS DEFINITIONS, stated as they are used. top3_finance: JF/JFE/RFS, last 24 months. strong_field: finance FIELD journals (JFQA, JCF, JBF, Financial Management, Real Estate Economics, JREFE, JFM, RCFS, JFI, RAPS), last 24 months -- the middle class, and the boundary where the top-3 threshold actually sits. stalled: finance field journals 24-48 months old with fewer than 5 citations -- published, old enough to have been noticed, and not noticed. That is NOT the 'never placed' construct the skill originally specified: SSRN carries that, and OpenAlex holds no abstracts for SSRN (0 of 125 sampled), so every Phase 3 field would be underivable. The substitute is labelled here rather than quietly swapped. KNOWN GAPS. Review of Finance is excluded: OpenAlex splits it across a 54-work record and its former name European Finance Review, so including it would add noise. 27 of the top3_finance entries came from an earlier themed pull on a single topic and carry that neighbourhood's slant. The 16 accounting acceptances and 17 out-of-scope 2026-06 stalled entries are kept with field_fit set, so an accounting-profile run keeps an anchor and a finance run filters them out; nothing was deleted. topic_area and mechanism are model judgments read from abstracts, carried per entry by calibration_confidence. REMAINING SHORTFALL, named rather than filled: the stalled class has only 2 household entries against a per-area floor of 4. Field journals in the 24-48 month window published few household-finance papers that went uncited, and the alternative was relabelling housing papers as household. The per-area flag in the Phase 5 report checks top3 and strong_field only, so this gap would otherwise pass unremarked.

papers.contribution_claim: The documented positive carbon return comes from forward-looking information in emissions released with a lag, not from ex ante expected returns.

papers.displacement_target: the documented positive carbon return premium in prior studies
papers.selection_bias_note: Global sample; the correction's size depends on the assumed release lag.

papers.title: Pricing Poseidon: Extreme Weather Uncertainty and Firm Return Dynamics
papers.question: How do markets price the uncertainty generated by an approaching extreme weather event?
papers.contribution_claim: Implied volatility jumps before landfall while the volatility risk premium shows investors underestimate the uncertainty, and idiosyncratic hurricanes still move expected returns.
papers.mechanism: salience-driven underreaction to firm-level physical risk, attenuating after a focal event
papers.displacement_target: the model claim that idiosyncratic shocks should not affect expected returns
papers.selection_bias_note: Hurricane forecasts are the treatment; the post-Sandy split is one event and is interpreted as salience.

papers.title: Pricing of sustainability-linked bonds
papers.question: What do investors pay for a sustainability-linked bond's ESG label, and are the targets real?
papers.contribution_claim: Investors accept 1-2bps for the label while issuers set targets that are 14-39% likely to be missed, and the market prices the penalty correctly.
papers.mechanism: label demand plus contingent-payoff pricing, with target difficulty chosen by the issuer
papers.displacement_target: claims that the sustainability-linked bond market is mispriced or that the greenium reflects impact alone
papers.selection_bias_note: Young market, small sample of issues; the probability-of-miss estimate carries model risk.

papers.title: Putting the Price in Asset Pricing
papers.question: How large is the gap between a portfolio's price and the present value its asset pricing model implies?
papers.contribution_claim: An abnormal-price estimator, built on a new identity, that plays the role for prices that abnormal returns play for returns.
papers.mechanism: long-horizon return decomposition separates risk from mispricing in the level rather than the change
papers.displacement_target: the convention of judging mispricing through abnormal returns rather than price levels
papers.selection_bias_note: A measurement contribution rather than an empirical finding; kept archetype-eligible because it proposes an estimand, not an econometric practice note.

papers.title: Forest through the Trees: Building Cross‐Sections of Stock Returns
papers.question: What is the right set of test assets for a given collection of characteristics?
papers.contribution_claim: Decision trees group stocks to span the SDF, giving interpretable low-dimensional cross-sections that beat many sorts out of sample.
papers.mechanism: endogenous portfolio splits replace ad hoc sorts, capturing characteristic interactions
papers.displacement_target: the convention of single and double sorts as the test assets of record
papers.selection_bias_note: Out-of-sample gains depend on the characteristic set supplied.

papers.title: Corporate Loan Spreads and Economic Activity
papers.question: Do secondary-market corporate loan spreads forecast the business cycle better than bond spreads?
papers.contribution_claim: A new loan-market credit spread outperforms existing credit-spread indicators, and supply-side frictions rather than borrower fundamentals drive the predictive power.
papers.mechanism: intermediary-reliant borrowers transmit lender balance-sheet frictions into prices before activity turns
papers.displacement_target: the bond-market excess-premium credit spread as the benchmark macro predictor
papers.selection_bias_note: Secondary loan prices are a new series; Lens 10 by construction, so the contribution rests on the mechanism split rather than the data alone.

papers.title: Mortgage Lock‐In, Mobility, and Labor Reallocation
papers.question: Does mortgage rate lock-in stop people moving, and does that hold back labor reallocation?
papers.contribution_claim: A 1pp lock-in gap cuts moving by 9% overall and 16% in 2022-24, and dampens responses to nearby job opportunities.
papers.mechanism: a below-market fixed rate is an asset lost on moving, so it taxes mobility asymmetrically
papers.displacement_target: the belief that rate lock-in is a nuisance for housing turnover without real labor-market consequences
papers.selection_bias_note: Housing-finance subject with household units; filed as household with housing and mortgage field tags rather than counted toward the thin real_estate class.

papers.title: Growing the efficient frontier on panel trees
papers.question: Can tree-based portfolios built from panel returns advance the efficient frontier?
papers.contribution_claim: P-Trees construct test assets and traded factors that push out the frontier and recover the pricing kernel with sparsity.
papers.mechanism: economically guided high-dimensional sorting on unbalanced panels
papers.displacement_target: observable and latent factor models as the benchmark pricing kernels
papers.selection_bias_note: Close in construction to W4413910745; the two are near-siblings and should not both be drawn as independent analogs.

papers.title: Risk-Free Rates and Convenience Yields Around the World
papers.question: How large are safe-asset convenience yields across currencies, and do they explain CIP deviations?
papers.contribution_claim: Option-implied risk-free rates give convenience yields for 10 G11 currencies, and CIP deviations measured against them are similar in size across countries.
papers.mechanism: domestic intermediary demand sets convenience yields while international arbitrageur funding sets CIP deviations
papers.displacement_target: the regularity that US convenience yields are exceptionally large and drive CIP deviations
papers.selection_bias_note: Option-implied rates require liquid index options, so the currency set is restricted to G11.

papers.title: Equilibrium Data Mining and Data Abundance
papers.question: How does an abundance of new data change the allocation of capital between quantitative and discretionary managers?
papers.contribution_claim: Data abundance can make data miners search less intensively, dispersing their performance and cutting their capital, while still raising price informativeness.
papers.mechanism: endogenous search intensity over predictor precision under a selection threshold
papers.displacement_target: the presumption that more data uniformly favours quantitative managers
papers.selection_bias_note: Theory only; no empirical test, so parity comparisons on identification are not meaningful for this entry.

papers.title: Green Window Dressing
papers.question: Do funds trade around disclosure dates to inflate their sustainability ratings?
papers.contribution_claim: ESG betas rise before disclosure and fall after, post-disclosure returns have lower ESG exposure than disclosed portfolios, and ESG stock prices move with the cycle.
papers.mechanism: window dressing against a rating measured at a known date
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that a fund's disclosed portfolio represents what it holds through the period
papers.selection_bias_note: Disclosure dates are known, so the test is sharp; the price effect is the weakest of the three findings.

papers.title: Persuading Investors: A Video‐Based Study
papers.question: Does how a startup pitch is delivered, rather than what it says, change funding outcomes?
papers.contribution_claim: Visual, vocal and verbal positivity raises funding probability while predicting worse post-funding performance, and the delivery penalty falls unevenly on women.
papers.mechanism: persuasion through delivery substitutes for information, so investors over-weight affect
papers.displacement_target: the convention that pitch content, not delivery, carries the information investors act on
papers.selection_bias_note: Machine-extracted delivery measures from video; the gender result rests on single-gender team subsamples.

papers.title: Financial Sophistication and Consumer Spending
papers.question: Do unsophisticated consumers respond to income changes they could have seen coming?
papers.contribution_claim: Controlling for liquidity, financially unsophisticated consumers still respond to predictable income decreases, and they hold thinner buffers.
papers.mechanism: limited financial sophistication rather than binding liquidity drives excess sensitivity
papers.displacement_target: the liquidity-constraint explanation for excess sensitivity of consumption to predictable income
papers.selection_bias_note: Account-level data from one provider; sophistication is proxied rather than assigned.

papers.title: Finance, Advertising, and Race
papers.question: Can bank advertising itself generate racial disparities in the products people hold?
papers.contribution_claim: A deregulation that let a bank misuse depositor funds raised advertising in African American newspapers and drew Black deposits into an insolvent institution, with persuasion as the traced channel.
papers.mechanism: targeted persuasion steers minority depositors toward inferior products
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that disparities in financial products come from demand or screening rather than from marketing
papers.selection_bias_note: Single historical institution; external validity to modern advertising is argued, not shown.

papers.title: When Financial Advice Leads to Positive Performance: Evidence from Repeated Client–Advisor Interactions
papers.question: Does the performance of an advisor's past recommendations bring the client back?
papers.contribution_claim: Positive performance on followed recommendations makes a second meeting 2.1 times more likely, so advice demand is experience-driven.
papers.mechanism: reinforcement from realized outcomes on the subset the investor acted on
papers.displacement_target: the view that advice-seeking is set by investor characteristics rather than by past advice outcomes
papers.selection_bias_note: One German brokerage, 2005-2015; whether the investor followed the advice is itself endogenous.

papers.title: Paying Too Much? Borrower Sophistication and Overpayment in the U.S. Mortgage Market
papers.question: How much do US mortgage borrowers overpay relative to what lenders would have offered them?
papers.contribution_claim: Overpayment is substantial and varies with borrower type and the rate environment, and expensive lenders are not delivering a better experience.
papers.mechanism: search and knowledge frictions leave rents on the table in a market with many lenders
papers.displacement_target: the presumption that lender competition in the US mortgage market competes rates down to a common frontier
papers.selection_bias_note: The counterfactual rate is constructed from lender pricing engines; overpayment is measured against that construction.

papers.title: New Frontiers in Household Finance
papers.question: n/a
papers.contribution_claim: Editorial introduction to a household finance special issue.
papers.mechanism: n/a
papers.displacement_target: none
papers.selection_bias_note: An editorial, not an empirical paper. Flagged archetype_eligible false: a parity comparison against a special-issue introduction measures nothing.

papers.title: Treasury Bill Shortages and the Pricing of Short‐Term Assets
papers.question: What sets short-term spreads in post-crisis money markets?
papers.contribution_claim: Capital regulation segments money markets, so the scarcity of T-bills available to shadow banks drives short-term spreads and open market operations can cut net liquidity.
papers.mechanism: regulation blocks banks from passing reserve liquidity to shadow banks, segmenting the market
papers.displacement_target: the model claim that reserve supply is the binding determinant of short-term spreads
papers.selection_bias_note: Quantitative model matched to post-2010 series; identification is the model's fit, not an experiment.

papers.title: Strategic arbitrage in segmented markets
papers.question: Why do obvious arbitrage opportunities go untaken in segmented markets?
papers.contribution_claim: With entry costs, arbitrageurs specialize strategically; only 57% of identified opportunities attract entry and half of those attract one arbitrageur.
papers.mechanism: repeated-game specialization sustains rents rather than competing them away
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that arbitrage capital moves to any positive-profit opportunity
papers.selection_bias_note: Unexercised-option arbitrage is one narrow setting chosen because the trades are identifiable.

papers.title: Intermediary Leverage Shocks and Funding Conditions
papers.question: Why does the price of intermediary leverage risk change sign across studies?
papers.contribution_claim: Separating leverage supply from leverage demand shocks resolves the sign puzzle and gives consistent evidence across markets.
papers.mechanism: supply shocks relax funding constraints while demand shocks tighten them, moving liquidity and returns opposite ways
papers.displacement_target: the conflicting estimates of the price of intermediary leverage risk in prior work
papers.selection_bias_note: Shock decomposition is identified by sign restrictions, so the resolution inherits those restrictions.

papers.title: Cross-Border M&A Flows, Economic Growth, and Foreign Exchange Rates
papers.question: Do cross-border M&A announcements carry information about future growth and exchange rates?
papers.contribution_claim: Domestic acquirers' decisions predict relative growth turning points and FX returns, consistent with heterogeneous-expectations exchange rate determination.
papers.mechanism: acquirers act on private views of local conditions, so their announcements reveal expectations
papers.displacement_target: the disconnect between exchange rates and macroeconomic fundamentals
papers.selection_bias_note: Predictive regressions on announcement flows; the model is described as simple and motivating rather than estimated.

papers.title: Economic policy uncertainty and institutional portfolio investment
papers.question: Does economic policy uncertainty reduce institutional holdings, at home and abroad?
papers.contribution_claim: EPU lowers institutional investment in domestic and overseas stocks, more so where destination countries are culturally distant.
papers.mechanism: uncertainty raises the cost of monitoring distant holdings
papers.displacement_target: none named beyond extending the EPU literature to institutional portfolios
papers.selection_bias_note: 28 markets over 21 years with an index-based regressor; a field-journal archetype of an association study without a sharp displacement target.

papers.title: Do Product Market Threats Discipline Corporate Misconduct?
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Does product market competition deter corporate misconduct?
papers.contribution_claim: Firms facing greater competitive threats commit fewer violations, pay lower penalties, and respond by strengthening ESG incentives and monitoring.
papers.mechanism: stakeholder punishment is amplified by competition, so the private cost of misconduct rises
papers.displacement_target: the view that misconduct is governed by internal governance rather than product market discipline
papers.selection_bias_note: Competitive threat is measured from text-based similarity; the deterrence channel is inferred from reactions, not assigned.

papers.title: Rookie directors and board efficacy
papers.question: Does appointing inexperienced directors weaken or strengthen the board?
papers.contribution_claim: Rookie refreshment improves monitoring — CEO turnover-performance sensitivity, incentives, earnings quality — without hurting advising.
papers.mechanism: new directors are less captured, so monitoring improves before experience accumulates
papers.displacement_target: the practitioner belief that rookie directors dilute board quality
papers.selection_bias_note: Board refreshment is endogenous to the firm's situation; the DEI-driven wave is used as context rather than as an instrument.

papers.title: Valuation and Long-Term Growth Expectations
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: What determines long-term growth expectations, and do prices reflect them?
papers.contribution_claim: Long-term growth is predictable from firm, industry and market characteristics, and prices do not fully capture it — high expected growth firms earn positive abnormal returns.
papers.mechanism: a valuation input with no established estimation convention is estimated, then tested against prices
papers.displacement_target: the absence of any convention for setting the terminal growth rate in valuation
papers.selection_bias_note: Estimated long-term growth is a generated regressor used in the return test.

papers.title: Competition and Debt Conservatism
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Does product market competition push firms toward zero leverage?
papers.contribution_claim: Competition raises zero-leverage propensity, and among three candidate explanations the flexibility motive is the one the evidence supports.
papers.mechanism: competitive pressure raises the option value of unused debt capacity
papers.displacement_target: the financial-constraint reading of zero-leverage firms
papers.selection_bias_note: Competition-law changes give the variation; the three-way horse race is decided on auxiliary predictions rather than a single test.

papers.title: Inalienable Human Capital and Inevitable Corporate Payouts
papers.question: Does the mobility of key employees change how firms split cash with shareholders?
papers.contribution_claim: Staggered rejections of the inevitable disclosure doctrine raise payouts, more so at human-capital-reliant firms.
papers.mechanism: more mobile talent bargains harder, and payouts commit cash away from that bargaining
papers.displacement_target: the treatment of payout policy as a shareholder-manager question with labor outside it
papers.selection_bias_note: IDD rejections across 15 states, a widely reused shock; treatment timing is staggered and the estimator's weighting matters.

papers.title: Intangible Value Creation Through Teamwork
papers.question: Does a collaboration culture correlate with intangible value creation?
papers.contribution_claim: Collaboration culture is positively associated with intangible value, with innovation and human capital as the channels.
papers.mechanism: stated as correlation with two mediating channels rather than an identified effect
papers.displacement_target: none named; the paper extends the corporate-culture literature to intangibles
papers.selection_bias_note: The abstract says correlates throughout and stacks fixed effects, PSM and DiD as robustness rather than as identification. A clear field-journal archetype of the no-displacement-target class.

papers.title: Block Diversity and Governance
papers.journal: The Review of Corporate Finance Studies
papers.question: Do financial and nonfinancial blockholders govern differently, and does that break a standard identification strategy?
papers.contribution_claim: Nonfinancial blocks govern through customized actions while financial blocks use generic metrics, and blockholdings correlate with Russell index-weight manipulation.
papers.mechanism: blockholder type determines the governance technology used
papers.displacement_target: the Russell index-threshold design as a clean instrument for institutional ownership
papers.selection_bias_note: The identification critique may prove more durable than the descriptive split; textual analysis of filings is the measure.

papers.title: A Trend Factor for the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Is there a trend factor that prices the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns?
papers.contribution_claim: CTREND aggregates price and volume signals across horizons, predicts returns, is not subsumed by known factors, and survives transaction costs.
papers.mechanism: technical signals aggregated by machine learning capture slow information diffusion
papers.displacement_target: existing crypto factor models as a complete description of the cross-section
papers.selection_bias_note: Lens 10 by construction: an established method on a new asset class. Survives costs, which is the check this archetype usually fails.

papers.title: Climate Adaptation Risk and Capital Structure: Evidence From State Climate Adaptation Plans
papers.question: Do state climate adaptation plans change corporate leverage?
papers.contribution_claim: Firms in states finalizing adaptation plans lever up more, driven by physical-risk-exposed firms, and the increase is value-enhancing.
papers.mechanism: public adaptation reduces business risk, which expands debt capacity
papers.displacement_target: none named beyond adding climate policy to the leverage determinants list
papers.selection_bias_note: Staggered state adoption used as a quasi-experiment; headquarters location proxies exposure.

papers.title: The Value of Investor Sophistication
papers.question: Can stock-level investor sophistication be measured, and does it price?
papers.contribution_claim: An idiosyncratic volatility spread proxies sophistication and is negatively related to returns, strongest where short-sale constraints bind.
papers.mechanism: sophisticated participation interacts with limits to arbitrage
papers.displacement_target: none named; positioned against the idiosyncratic-volatility puzzle without displacing an explanation
papers.selection_bias_note: A new proxy built from a variable already known to predict returns; the separation from the IVOL puzzle is asserted through controls.

papers.title: Investor Attention and Insider Trading
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do insiders trade against attention-driven mispricing?
papers.contribution_claim: Insiders sell into heightened retail attention and buy as it fades, most strongly in lottery-type and retail-heavy stocks, extending to seasoned equity issuance.
papers.mechanism: insiders time transactions against predictable retail attention cycles
papers.displacement_target: the information-based reading of insider trading profits
papers.selection_bias_note: Attention proxies include Robinhood herding episodes, a period-specific measure.

papers.title: Carbon transition risk and corporate loan securitization
papers.question: Do banks offload carbon transition risk by securitizing loans to polluting borrowers?
papers.contribution_claim: Banks securitize brown loans when transition risk is high and retain them when it falls, using the 2016 election as the shock.
papers.mechanism: regulatory arbitrage moves exposure to less regulated shadow banks
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that bank climate exposure can be read off the balance sheet
papers.selection_bias_note: One election as the shock, with everything else that changed at the same time.

papers.title: Returns from liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets
papers.question: What predicts the return to providing liquidity in cryptocurrency markets?
papers.contribution_claim: Short-reversal returns proxy the liquidity provision premium and are predictable from volatility, risk aversion, tail risk and Tether liquidity innovations.
papers.mechanism: compensation for inventory and adverse selection rises as liquidity withdraws
papers.displacement_target: none named; imports the short-reversal liquidity measure into crypto
papers.selection_bias_note: Lens 10 archetype; the Uniswap evidence is corroborative rather than identifying.

papers.title: Media coverage and the cost of equity capital around the world
papers.question: Does media coverage lower the implied cost of equity, internationally?
papers.contribution_claim: First global-scale evidence that media coverage reduces implied cost of equity, conditional on press freedom and outlet credibility.
papers.mechanism: coverage reduces information asymmetry, and the effect scales with the credibility of the source
papers.displacement_target: none; the claim is first-at-global-scale rather than a displacement
papers.selection_bias_note: Textbook setting_variation_only archetype: an established US result extended to 38 countries. Implied cost of capital is a model-derived dependent variable.

papers.title: Product Market Threats and Leases
papers.question: Do firms lease more when product markets threaten them?
papers.contribution_claim: Product market threats raise leasing, robust across four sources of plausibly exogenous variation, strongest among constrained firms.
papers.mechanism: leasing preserves flexibility and shifts residual risk when competitive pressure rises
papers.displacement_target: none named; extends the product-market-threat literature to the lease-buy margin
papers.selection_bias_note: Four shocks stacked as robustness rather than one design; a field-journal pattern where breadth substitutes for a sharp target.

papers.title: Securities Lending and Trading by Active and Passive Funds
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do mutual funds read information out of the securities lending market?
papers.contribution_claim: Active funds rebalance away from borrowed stocks whose prices fall while passive funds do not, and the spillover runs within fund families.
papers.mechanism: lending desks observe informed borrowing and the information travels inside the family
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that a fund's lending desk and its trading desk are informationally separate
papers.selection_bias_note: Family cooperativeness is a constructed moderator; the information channel is inferred from trade timing.

papers.title: Institutional Liquidity Costs, Internalized Retail Trade Imbalances, and the Cross Section of Stock Returns
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: What do institutions pay for liquidity when retail order flow is internalized away from them?
papers.contribution_claim: An institutional liquidity cost measure built from internalized retail imbalances prices the cross-section.
papers.mechanism: segmentation forces institutions onto expensive wholesaler-provided liquidity
papers.displacement_target: the treatment of retail internalization as a retail-side phenomenon with no institutional cost
papers.selection_bias_note: The measure is an average absolute imbalance; its mapping to a cost is posited rather than estimated.

papers.title: Visible Hands: Professional Asset Managers’ Expectations and the Stock Market in China
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do professional managers' growth expectations move their allocations and prices?
papers.contribution_claim: Pessimistic Chinese fund managers cut equity and shift away from cyclicals, and their expectations link to returns on the stocks they trade.
papers.mechanism: subjective growth expectations translate into portfolio tilts that move prices
papers.displacement_target: none named; brings novel expectations data to an established question
papers.selection_bias_note: Lens 10 archetype on a novel Chinese dataset; the price-informativeness result is the more transportable half.

papers.title: Government Investment Stimulus and Household Balance Sheet Externalities
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do corporate investment incentives spill over onto worker balance sheets?
papers.contribution_claim: Accelerated depreciation raises layoff risk for routine workers and cuts their risky asset share, with unemployment insurance mitigating the effect.
papers.mechanism: capital-labor substitution raises background risk, which crowds out household risk-taking
papers.displacement_target: the evaluation of investment stimulus on firm outcomes alone
papers.selection_bias_note: Links two literatures through individual-level data; routine-task exposure is a constructed classification.

papers.title: Shopping around: Empirical analysis of borrower comparison shopping and mortgage prices
papers.question: How many mortgage borrowers shop, and what does shopping save them?
papers.contribution_claim: Few borrowers shop; those who do save about 11 basis points, and both incidence and benefit differ by race.
papers.mechanism: search frictions with unequal returns to search across groups
papers.displacement_target: none named; documents a market friction on the universe of mortgages
papers.selection_bias_note: Shopping is inferred from a novel identification approach on credit inquiries, not observed directly.

papers.title: Pandemics and Household Cash Withdrawals: Evidence From Transaction Data on Hundreds of Millions of Bank Cards
papers.question: Did the pandemic permanently reduce cash use?
papers.contribution_claim: Cash transactions fell after the outbreak across 165 million cards and stayed low after the health concern passed.
papers.mechanism: a transitory shock shifted a habit, and the shift persisted
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: Very large but single-country administrative sample; the persistence claim rests on the post-period alone. A clear incremental_data_extension archetype.

papers.title: Predatory Lending and Hidden Risks
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Can predatory steering be identified from rapid reject-then-approve sequences by the same lender?
papers.contribution_claim: Steered borrowers are less sophisticated, get non-amortizing high-margin contracts that are quickly securitized, and default later rather than sooner.
papers.mechanism: lenders steer identifiable borrowers into contracts whose risk is passed on
papers.displacement_target: the difficulty of separating predatory steering from ordinary risk-based pricing
papers.selection_bias_note: The reject-then-approve signature is the paper's construct; whether it captures steering rather than re-underwriting is the open question.

papers.title: Granular risks and stock returns: Evidence from commercial real estate
papers.question: Do idiosyncratic commercial real estate shocks aggregate into stock market returns?
papers.contribution_claim: First empirical evidence of a causal link from granular property risks, arising from city size and dispersion, to stock returns.
papers.mechanism: Gabaix granularity: large, concentrated units fail to diversify away at the aggregate
papers.displacement_target: the granular-origins framework's untested application to property markets
papers.selection_bias_note: Causal is claimed in the abstract on a constructed aggregated measure; the causal language is stronger than the design.

papers.title: Property Market Liquidity and Secured or Unsecured Debt
papers.journal: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
papers.question: Does the liquidity of the underlying property market shape secured versus unsecured borrowing?
papers.contribution_claim: REITs exposed to more liquid property markets use more unsecured debt, estimated with an instrumental variables design.
papers.mechanism: liquid collateral is worth less as a pledge because the lender's outside option is already good
papers.displacement_target: the collateral-channel prediction that liquid assets support more secured debt
papers.selection_bias_note: REITs make asset liquidity observable, which is why the test is possible and why it may not generalize.

papers.title: Human mobility and commercial real estate: Evidence from REIT operating performance
papers.question: How did the pandemic shift in human mobility affect commercial real estate performance?
papers.contribution_claim: Predicted local mobility explains REIT operating performance, controlling for other pandemic factors.
papers.mechanism: mobility determines the demand that occupies space
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: Mobility is machine-learning predicted then used as a regressor, a generated-regressor problem the abstract does not address.

papers.title: The Transmission of Climate Hazard Exposure to Equity Risk: Evidence From Real Estate Firms
papers.journal: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
papers.question: Does physical climate hazard exposure raise the systematic risk of firms tied to physical assets?
papers.contribution_claim: Asset-location-level hazard exposure raises real estate firms' market beta through debt costs, earnings volatility and disaster-related capex.
papers.mechanism: hazard exposure at the asset level transmits into the firm's cost of capital
papers.displacement_target: the hypothesis that climate hazard exposure raises systematic rather than idiosyncratic risk
papers.selection_bias_note: 141 firms with ZIP-level hazard data; the sample is small and the channel decomposition is correlational.

papers.title: Aggregate Investment, Economic Dynamics, and Predictability In the REIT Market
papers.journal: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
papers.question: Does aggregate REIT investment predict REIT market returns?
papers.contribution_claim: A one-standard-deviation rise in aggregate operating asset growth signals about 5.6% lower expected annual excess REIT return over 1972-2023.
papers.mechanism: the q-theory investment-return link, applied to a sector where assets are observable
papers.displacement_target: none named; extends the aggregate-investment predictability result to REITs
papers.selection_bias_note: Long sample, single sector, one predictor; the setting_variation_only archetype with an unusually long time series.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Real Estate Agents and the Housing Cycle
papers.question: Does the quality of real estate agents shape the housing cycle?
papers.contribution_claim: Listings by inexperienced agents are less likely to sell, most sharply in the bust, and 3.7% more listings would have sold under flexible commissions.
papers.mechanism: fixed commissions plus free entry hold inexperienced intermediaries in the market, and their share rises when it matters most
papers.displacement_target: the treatment of housing intermediaries as a frictionless matching layer
papers.selection_bias_note: 8.5 million listings with a stated novel design; the counterfactual commission equilibrium is a model output, not an observation.

papers.title: Household mobility and mortgage rate lock
papers.question: Did rising rates lock homeowners into their houses?
papers.contribution_claim: Mobility fell in 2022-23 for homeowners with mortgages, absolutely and relative to mortgage-free owners, as market rates rose.
papers.mechanism: a below-market fixed rate is an asset forfeited on moving, so it taxes housing turnover
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that mortgage rate lock is a pricing curiosity rather than a constraint on housing turnover
papers.selection_bias_note: Mortgage-free owners are the comparison group and differ on wealth and age; the episode is one rate cycle.

papers.title: Competition, Product differentiation and Crises: Evidence from 18 million securitized loans
papers.question: Did competition among securitizers shape the mortgage contracts borrowers were offered?
papers.contribution_claim: A regulatory shock to sponsor competition shows securitization feeding back into loan design, with prime collateral differentiating faster than non-prime in the early boom.
papers.mechanism: sponsors differentiate the derived security by differentiating the underlying loan
papers.displacement_target: the treatment of securitization as a channel that transmits risk without shaping the asset it packages
papers.selection_bias_note: 18 million loans and a named regulatory shock; the feedback claim rests on timing across prime and non-prime segments.

papers.title: Price and Volume Divergence in China’s Real Estate Markets: The Role of Local Governments
papers.question: Why did Chinese house prices rise while transaction volumes collapsed?
papers.contribution_claim: Local governments managed prices through supply controls, LGFV land purchases and sales-permit limits, and cities more dependent on land revenue show greater price-volume divergence.
papers.mechanism: a fiscally motivated seller intervenes to defend price, which trades volume for price
papers.displacement_target: the reading of price-volume divergence as a demand or expectations phenomenon
papers.selection_bias_note: Cross-city variation in pre-pandemic land dependence carries the identification; institutionally specific to China.

papers.title: FinTech vs. Bank: The impact of lending technology on credit market competition
papers.question: How does lending technology divide the business loan market between FinTechs and banks?
papers.contribution_claim: A model with heterogeneous screening ability and borrower horizons predicts FinTechs supply unsecured short-horizon loans and traditional lenders asset-backed long-horizon ones.
papers.mechanism: screening technology and collateral interact to segment borrowers by project horizon
papers.displacement_target: the framing of FinTech entry as undifferentiated competition for the same borrowers
papers.selection_bias_note: Primarily theoretical; the empirical content in the abstract is limited to consistency checks.

papers.title: What Is Fueling FinTech Lending? The Role of Banking Market Structure
papers.journal: The Review of Corporate Finance Studies
papers.question: What explains where FinTech lending grows?
papers.contribution_claim: FinTech penetration in small business lending is higher where large or out-of-market banks are more present, isolating incumbent technology as the driver.
papers.mechanism: FinTechs fill the gap left where incumbents use transaction rather than relationship technology
papers.displacement_target: the regulatory-arbitrage explanation for FinTech lending growth
papers.selection_bias_note: Small business lending is chosen because the technologies are comparable; that choice also bounds the generalization.

papers.title: Open data and API adoption of U.S. banks
papers.question: Which banks adopt external APIs, and what happens when they announce it?
papers.contribution_claim: US banks adopting APIs from 2007-2022 are larger and face less competitive pressure, with announcement effects reported.
papers.mechanism: data portability is adopted where scale absorbs the fixed cost and competition does not force it
papers.displacement_target: none named; documents adoption determinants for a new technology
papers.selection_bias_note: An adoption-determinants study on a new technology; the pattern found is the one size and competition usually produce.

papers.title: Where Have All the IPOs Gone? Trade Liberalization and the Changing Nature of U.S. Public Corporations
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Did trade liberalization with China change the rate at which US firms go and stay public?
papers.contribution_claim: A tariff policy change lowered public listing rates and raised concentration, blocking entry by small domestic manufacturers while leaving multinationals unharmed.
papers.mechanism: import competition shifts the entry calculus asymmetrically by firm size
papers.displacement_target: none named; the results are reported as consistent with heterogeneous-firm trade models
papers.selection_bias_note: Good identification on a crowded question. Consistent-with is not displacement, and the listing-decline literature already had several explanations.

papers.title: Credit Default Swaps and Firm Cyclicality
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Does the arrival of CDS trading change how cyclical a borrower's business becomes?
papers.contribution_claim: Firm cyclicality falls 40% after CDS inception, driven by less aggressive asset growth in good times and strongest under the empty-creditor problem.
papers.mechanism: credit insurance hardens the creditor, which disciplines expansion in booms
papers.displacement_target: debt overhang and bank-lending cyclicality as the explanations for the pattern, both ruled out
papers.selection_bias_note: CDS inception is endogenous and the abstract handles it with a phrase; the empty-creditor moderator is the strongest part.

papers.title: Friendly Investing and Information Sharing in the Asset Management Industry
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do funds invest favourably in connected financial groups to buy access to information?
papers.contribution_claim: Broker-connected funds overweight the connected group's stock and vote with management, and their performance improves.
papers.mechanism: quid pro quo: friendly capital and friendly votes bought with privileged information
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that a fund's voting and its brokerage relationships are independent
papers.selection_bias_note: Connections proxied by broker relationships; the information channel is inferred from performance rather than observed.

papers.title: Main bank impairment and corporate cash holdings during the global financial crisis
papers.question: Do firms hoard cash when their main bank is impaired?
papers.contribution_claim: Japanese firms whose main banks were impaired in 2008 raised cash holdings, more so among bank-dependent firms.
papers.mechanism: precautionary saving against an anticipated loss of credit access
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: The bank-lending channel in Japan in 2008 on 2,520 firms; an established design in a well-studied setting.

papers.title: Partisanship, optimism, and firm innovation
papers.question: Do executives politically aligned with the president innovate more?
papers.contribution_claim: Firms whose managers share the president's party show higher patent counts, citations and value, identified around elections.
papers.mechanism: partisan optimism raises willingness to invest in uncertain projects
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: Alignment is measured from donations; why partisan optimism would raise patent value rather than patent count is not separated.

papers.title: Assessing and mitigating fire sales risk under partial information
papers.question: How well can fire-sale risk be assessed when the regulator sees only part of the holdings matrix?
papers.contribution_claim: Compares matrix reconstruction methods on EBA stress-test data and evaluates which policy interventions survive partial information.
papers.mechanism: overlapping portfolios propagate forced selling, and the propagation depends on what the reconstruction gets wrong
papers.displacement_target: the implicit assumption that fire-sale models can be applied to the partial data regulators actually hold
papers.selection_bias_note: A methodological comparison; the payoff is a caveat about existing models rather than a finding a referee can act on.

papers.title: A New Value Strategy
papers.journal: The Review of Asset Pricing Studies
papers.question: Can value be rescued by a better price scaler?
papers.contribution_claim: Cash-based operating profitability over price earns 0.78-1.04% monthly and survives in large caps.
papers.mechanism: a cleaner numerator removes the accrual noise that broke book-to-market
papers.displacement_target: book-to-market as the value measure of record
papers.selection_bias_note: A new ratio in a crowded factor zoo; the abstract reports returns without an out-of-sample or post-publication test.

papers.title: Anomalies, option volume, and disagreement
papers.question: Do anomaly returns strengthen when option volume signals disagreement?
papers.contribution_claim: Anomaly returns are amplified when disagreement-driven option volume is high before earnings announcements.
papers.mechanism: biased beliefs are corrected around announcements, and option volume reveals them
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: Disagreement volume is a constructed split of option volume; the amplification is an interaction on known anomalies.

papers.title: Corporate Financial Frictions and Employee Mental Health
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do a firm's financing frictions reach its employees' health?
papers.contribution_claim: Firms needing to refinance in 2008 show higher employee antidepressant use, using administrative microdata.
papers.mechanism: financial distress transmits to workers as job insecurity and effort pressure
papers.displacement_target: none named; extends the real-effects-of-finance literature to a health outcome
papers.selection_bias_note: Sharp design and a genuinely novel outcome; the maturity-structure instrument is heavily reused and was contested after 2008.

papers.title: Demand for financial advice: Evidence from a randomized choice experiment
papers.question: Does making advice fees salient and upfront reduce demand for financial advice?
papers.contribution_claim: In a randomized choice experiment on 2,100 Dutch panellists, a fee-based regime lowers demand for advice relative to commissions.
papers.mechanism: salient upfront costs are weighted more heavily than embedded commissions
papers.displacement_target: the presumption that a commission ban improves consumer outcomes by making costs transparent
papers.selection_bias_note: Hypothetical choices in a survey panel standing in for a real mortgage decision.

papers.title: Predicting Returns Out of Sample: A Naïve Model Averaging Approach
papers.journal: The Review of Asset Pricing Studies
papers.question: How should out-of-sample return forecasts be combined with the historical mean?
papers.contribution_claim: A naive average of the OLS forecast and the historical mean produces positive out-of-sample R2, and more sophisticated weightings do not beat it.
papers.mechanism: shrinkage toward the mean under unstable relations and short samples
papers.displacement_target: sophisticated forecast-combination schemes as an improvement over simple averaging
papers.selection_bias_note: A methods contribution in an asset-pricing journal; the surprising half is a negative result about complexity, which is easy to under-sell.

papers.title: The Only Constant Is Change: Nonconstant Volatility and Implied Volatility Spreads
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Is implied volatility spread predictability real, or an artifact of time-varying volatility?
papers.contribution_claim: Volatility spreads arise under no-arbitrage for American options when volatility varies, and the predictability changes systematically with aggregate volatility.
papers.mechanism: firms' sensitivities to aggregate volatility generate the spread mechanically
papers.displacement_target: the informed-trading interpretation of volatility-spread return predictability
papers.selection_bias_note: A debunking result whose value depends on the reader having believed the original; those are systematically under-cited.

papers.title: Chinese exclusion? Agent response in the market for owner‐occupied housing
papers.question: Do real estate agents respond differently to Chinese and white clients?
papers.contribution_claim: A correspondence experiment finds no differential response in the full sample, with significant differences in rural areas and some states.
papers.mechanism: agent screening on ethnicity where market thinness raises the return to selection
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: A clean audit design whose headline is a null; the subsample findings carry the paper and are the least powered part of it.

papers.title: Risk perception in housing markets: Evidence from a fighter jet crash
papers.question: Does a salient accident change how housing prices capitalize a risk that was already disclosed?
papers.contribution_claim: Prices near a Virginia naval air station move after a jet crash despite the hazard having been disclosed for years.
papers.mechanism: salience rather than information changes the price of a known risk
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that disclosed risks are already capitalized
papers.selection_bias_note: One crash, one base, one metro; the design is sharp and the sample is a single event.

papers.title: How Do Cash Windfalls Affect Entrepreneurship? Evidence from the Spanish Christmas Lottery
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do household cash windfalls create businesses?
papers.contribution_claim: Spanish Christmas Lottery wins raise start-up entry, job creation and self-employment, strongest where financial constraints bind.
papers.mechanism: a wealth shock relaxes the constraint on entry
papers.displacement_target: none named beyond confirming a financial-constraints channel
papers.selection_bias_note: The Christmas Lottery is a well-worn instrument; the design is clean and the question has been asked with other windfalls.

papers.title: Do Directors Respond to Stock Mispricing? Evidence from CEO Turnovers
papers.journal: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.question: Do boards fire CEOs for price movements that carry no information?
papers.contribution_claim: A one-standard-deviation uninformative negative price shock raises CEO turnover by 10%, more at independent boards.
papers.mechanism: boards cannot fully filter noise from price signals when evaluating the CEO
papers.displacement_target: the assumption that boards condition on fundamentals rather than on price
papers.selection_bias_note: Uninformative is defined by a decomposition, so the result is only as clean as that split; 1,573 firms.

papers.title: Deciphering the U.S. metropolitan house price dynamics
papers.question: Can house price forecasts be improved by allowing cross-sectional heterogeneity and dependence?
papers.contribution_claim: A new heterogeneous estimator forecasts county house prices across 56 metro areas better than the alternatives.
papers.mechanism: metros differ in their price dynamics and are not independent of one another
papers.displacement_target: homogeneous-panel forecasting methods for house prices
papers.selection_bias_note: A forecasting-method paper; the economics is in the estimator rather than in the housing market.

papers.title: Down payment requirements and house prices: Quasi‐experiment evidence from Shanghai
papers.question: What does a higher down payment requirement do to house prices?
papers.contribution_claim: A regression discontinuity at Shanghai's Inner Ring, where the minimum down payment jumps from 50% to 70%, gives a causal price effect.
papers.mechanism: a binding leverage constraint shifts the marginal buyer and therefore the price
papers.displacement_target: none named beyond establishing causality for a widely assumed relationship
papers.selection_bias_note: A genuinely sharp discontinuity in one city; the local nature of an RD at a ring road is both its strength and its ceiling.

papers.title: Top‐floor discounts in residential buildings: Evidence from South Korea
papers.question: Do top-floor apartments sell at a discount, and why?
papers.contribution_claim: Top-floor discounts of 1.3-8.3% across 1.9 million Korean resale transactions, attributed to heating and cooling costs.
papers.mechanism: a physical attribute maps into running costs and then into price
papers.displacement_target: none named
papers.selection_bias_note: Textbook setting_variation_only: a hedonic regularity documented in one country. The cost mechanism is hypothesized, not tested against alternatives.

papers.title: Two-worker Households, Decentralized Employment, and Residential Segregation
papers.journal: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
papers.question: How do two-earner households change residential sorting and segregation?
papers.contribution_claim: A Tiebout model extended to two-worker households, letting residential and labor choices be made jointly.
papers.mechanism: joint commuting constraints alter the sorting equilibrium
papers.displacement_target: the single-earner assumption in Hybrid Tiebout models
papers.selection_bias_note: A model extension whose empirical content is limited; relaxing an assumption is not by itself a displacement.
